method: Structured JSON from the Gemini API, instructed by docs/PROJECT_VISION.md@main blob fe2f414774b7. Every cited URL was fetched; dead links and pages that never mention the character were removed, and feats, results, conditions and campaign tags that lost their source were moved to unknowns. All records provisional.

characters.continuity: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos and The Frozen Throne, from taking Frostmourne in Northrend until he reached the Frozen Throne
characters.summary: Death knight Arthas fights with the soul-stealing runeblade Frostmourne and necromantic power drawn from the Lich King. In this era he killed Uther and his father Terenas and defeated Illidan at Icecrown.

techniques: Frostmourne strikes; the blade steals souls
Necromancy: raised his dead horse Invincible into undeath

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Sylvanas shot him with a paralyzing arrow
His power faltered as the Lich King's power waned; he suffered a seizure while fighting in Lordaeron
limitations: His power depended on the Lich King's; it was replenished only when Ner'zhul restored it in Azjol-Nerub
characters.formDifferences: Arthas after taking up Frostmourne and serving the Lich King as a death knight, before he donned Ner'zhul's helm. The Stratholme purge came earlier, while he was still a paladin, and is not part of this form.

sources.supports: Death knight era: killing Uther at Andorhal and Terenas in Lordaeron, the Illidan duel at Icecrown, raising Invincible, the waning of his power, and Sylvanas's paralyzing arrow

feats.claim: Ran Frostmourne through his father King Terenas's heart
Raised his horse Invincible into undeath at Balnir Farmstead

notableResults.citation: Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos, Andorhal
notableResults.note: Uther knocked Frostmourne from his hands before Arthas recovered it and struck the killing blow

notableResults.citation: Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne, Icecrown
notableResults.note: Illidan left himself open and Arthas slashed his chest; he took Illidan's dagger Stormfury

campaignTags.claim: Rides his raised undead horse Invincible

unknowns: Named Warcraft III death knight abilities (Death Coil, Death Pact, Animate Dead) are not on the cited page; not claimed

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Gemini's Stratholme feat belongs to his paladin era and was removed. The 'urn' detail in the Uther result is not in the source. `magic` and `spellcaster` were removed because the page names no death knight spells; `magic-item` and `mount` were added.

conditional.dependsOn: The Lich King's strength, which was waning in this period

characters.continuity: World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King (Arthas as the Lich King, ending at Icecrown Citadel)
characters.summary: The Lich King commands frost and shadow magic, plagues and the risen dead. At the climax of the Icecrown Citadel fight, Fury of Frostmourne kills the entire raid; he is beaten only after Tirion shatters Frostmourne.

techniques: Soul Reaper (delayed heavy shadow strike on his main foe)
Defile (spreading, growing shadow pool)
Remorseless Winter (45-yard frost storm)
Necrotic Plague and Infest
Ice Sphere / Ice Burst knockback
Summon Val'kyr to carry foes off the platform
Harvest Soul (pulls survivors into Frostmourne)
Raise Dead
Fury of Frostmourne (kills all enemies and blocks resurrection)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Shattering Frostmourne frees the trapped souls, which immobilize him
Arrogance: he gloats over his fallen foes, and at the Wrathgate revealing himself exposed him to Putress's plague
characters.formDifferences: Arthas after donning Ner'zhul's helm and becoming the Lich King, still wielding Frostmourne, as fought in Icecrown Citadel.

sources.supports: Icecrown Citadel abilities (Soul Reaper, Defile, Remorseless Winter, Necrotic Plague, Infest, Ice Sphere, Val'kyr, Harvest Soul, Raise Dead, Fury of Frostmourne) and the ending in which Tirion shatters Frostmourne
Ner'zhul's helm, freezing Tirion, the arrogance at the Wrathgate, and his death

feats.claim: Fury of Frostmourne killed every member of the attacking raid and prevented their resurrection, until Terenas's spirit revived them
feats.citation: WoW: Wrath of the Lich King, Icecrown Citadel

feats.claim: Froze Tirion Fordring in ice during the final battle
feats.citation: WoW: Wrath of the Lich King, Icecrown Citadel

notableResults.opponent: Tirion Fordring and the heroes of Azeroth
notableResults.citation: WoW: Wrath of the Lich King, Icecrown Citadel
notableResults.note: Tirion shattered Frostmourne with the Ashbringer; the freed souls immobilized him and the revived raid finished him

campaignTags.claim: Casts Defile, Remorseless Winter, Necrotic Plague, Raise Dead and Fury of Frostmourne
Remorseless Winter frost storm and Ice Sphere frost bursts
Wields Frostmourne and wears Ner'zhul's helm

unknowns: Encounter numbers (e.g. 1,000,000 damage) are game mechanics and should not be read as literal lore scaling

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): the cited page (wowpedia /wiki/The_Lich_King) never came up in a search and was not opened. It is replaced with Lich King (tactics) and Arthas Menethil, both opened. Removed as unsupported: 'immunity to biological vulnerabilities', 'magical barriers', frostwyrm flight, and '25 champions'. Arrogance is now a weakness instead of a limitation. The broad `magic` and `ice` tags are narrowed to `spellcaster` and `ice-control`, and `magic-item` was added.

conditional.ability: Freedom of action in the final phase
conditional.dependsOn: Frostmourne remaining intact; its destruction freed souls that immobilized him

characters.continuity: Pokémon anime (Pokémon the Series, through Pokémon Journeys)
characters.summary: A Trainer who battles by commanding his Pokémon with a versatile, unpredictable style. He uses type matchups and the environment, and turns opponents' moves against them. He became Alola's first Champion and the World Coronation Series Monarch.

techniques: Commands his Pokémon, exploiting type advantages and the environment
Turns opponents' moves against them (Lycanroc vs Gladion's Counter)
Z-Moves, including Pikachu's 10,000,000 Volt Thunderbolt with his self-made Pikashunium Z
Mega Evolution with Lucario
Bond Phenomenon with Greninja (XY)
Dynamax and Gigantamax, including Gigantamax Pikachu without a Poké Ball

mechanisms: Can survive Pokémon attacks for long periods without much damage, depending on the situation

weaknesses: Not established by the cited source
limitations: His offense comes through the Pokémon he commands

sources.supports: Battle style, Z-Moves, Mega Evolution, Dynamax/Gigantamax, durability, and league results (Manalo Conference champion, Monarch after beating Leon, Lumiose runner-up to Alain)

feats.claim: Won the Manalo Conference and became the Alola League's first Champion
Won the Masters Eight Tournament and became Monarch

notableResults.citation: Pokémon Journeys, World Coronation Series final
Pokémon the Series: Sun & Moon, Manalo Conference final
Pokémon the Series: XY, Lumiose Conference final
Pokémon: Diamond and Pearl, Sinnoh League semifinal

unknowns: Owner ruling needed: should a Trainer earn tags (e.g. electric) for powers that belong to his Pokémon?

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Bulbapedia's Ash Ketchum and Ash's achievements pages failed to load, so they were replaced by the Pokémon Wiki page, which was opened. Removed as unsupported: 'Pokémon intercept attacks', the 'vulnerable if separated' weakness, and running or riding mobility (the page says only Pikachu rides on him). `electric` and `electric-control` were removed because they are Pikachu's powers, pending a ruling.

characters.continuity: God of War (2018) and God of War Ragnarök (2022), Norse saga
characters.summary: Kratos's son. He fights with the Talon Bow and magic-imbued arrows, summoned Jörmungandr by speaking the Jötnar language, and in Ragnarök shapeshifts into a wolf and the massive bear Björn.

techniques: Talon Bow archery
Lightning-imbued bow and mistletoe arrows (2018)
Light, Sonic and Sigil-imbued arrows (Ragnarök)
Summoned Jörmungandr by speaking the Jötnar language
Shapeshifting into a wolf, and into the massive bear Björn
Spartan Rage (first triggered against Modi)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: Illness: strong emotions bring on coughing fits and can make him pass out (2018)
Blinding rage and loss of control; as Björn he rampaged until Kratos subdued him
Overconfident and reckless after learning of his godhood
Outclassed by Heimdall, who deflected his attacks and caught his arrow
limitations: His transformations are triggered by panic or overwhelming emotion rather than chosen freely (Ragnarök)

sources.supports: Talon Bow and imbued arrows, summoning Jörmungandr, shapeshifting, Spartan Rage, fights with Modi, Baldur and Heimdall, and his illness, rage and overconfidence

feats.claim: Summoned Jörmungandr in the Jötnar language during the fight with Baldur
Transformed into the massive bear Björn and rampaged until Kratos beat him back to human form

notableResults.citation: God of War (2018)
notableResults.note: Modi had already been beaten and was injured

campaignTags.claim: Summoned Jörmungandr by speaking the Jötnar language; uses runic and Sigil magic through his bow

unknowns: Outcome of Odin's defeat: the page excerpt credits Atreus with extracting Odin's soul, but Ragnarök's finale was a group effort. No result is recorded.

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Removed as unsupported: Gemini's win over Thrúd (the page has her hold him at swordpoint and then befriend him), 'magical barriers' (the page's barrier is the home grove's protective ward), evasion, the strength limitation, and running and climbing. The broad `magic` tag was removed in favor of `spellcaster`. Page read to about 100k of 126k characters.

characters.summary: An Umbra Witch who combines Bullet Arts gunplay with hair-summoned demons (Wicked Weaves), Enochian Torture Attacks and Witch Time. She sent Jubileus into the sun, and she was overpowered by Loptr and by Singularity Definition.

techniques: Bullet Arts
Wicked Weaves: hair-summoned demon limbs
Infernal Weaves: full demon finishers during Umbran Climax
Torture Attacks summoned by Enochian chanting
Demon Slave: summons and directs Infernal Demons (Bayonetta 3)
Demon Masquerade: humanoid demon forms (Bayonetta 3)
Freezes moisture in the air into a spear

mechanisms: Witch Time: slows time around her; counters a Sage's Light Speed and can be stacked against another witch or an angel
Superhuman perception that anticipates enemy movements

weaknesses: Her Umbran Watch is essential; its breaking led to her death (Bayonetta 3)
Fixed in place and vulnerable while controlling a Demon Slave summon
Overpowered by Loptr and Singularity Definition; weakened after a Deadly Sin ritual
mobility: Witch Walk on walls and ceilings (conditional)
Beast Within: crow and panther forms
limitations: Her normal attacks struggled against big bosses (the reason Serious Mode was created)
Witch Walk works only under a full moon or on certain devices made by Aesir

sources.supports: Bullet Arts, Wicked and Infernal Weaves, Torture Attacks, Witch Time, Beast Within, Witch Walk, demon summoning, and fights with Jubileus, Balder, Loptr, Aesir and Singularity

feats.claim: Summoned Queen Sheba with Jeanne's help and sent Jubileus hurtling into the sun
Redirected a satellite at Aesir using only her lower body

notableResults.citation: Bayonetta (2009)
Bayonetta (2009), Ithavoll Tower
Bayonetta 2
notableResults.note: Beaten in their first fight; at Fimbulventr he subdued her and took the Left Eye

notableResults.citation: Bayonetta 3
notableResults.note: She fell to Singularity Definition; Luka and Gomorrah destroyed him, and she died when her Umbran Watch broke

campaignTags.claim: Summons Torture Attacks by Enochian chanting and summons demons through Wicked Weaves
Freezes moisture in the air into a spear

unknowns: Whether her crow form flies: the page does not describe flight explicitly, so natural-flight is not proposed

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): the cited /wiki/Bayonetta URL never came up in search; the character page /wiki/Bayonetta_(character) was opened instead. Gemini's 'punched Jubileus into the sun' is corrected: Queen Sheba did it, with Jeanne's help. Removed: 'magical barriers' and the Witch Time trigger limitation (not on the page). The broad `magic` and `natural-flight` tags were removed; `ice-control` was added.

characters.continuity: Metal Gear series: Naked Snake / Big Boss himself (MGS3: Snake Eater through Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake), not Venom Snake
characters.summary: Legendary soldier who trained under The Boss, matched her CQC mastery, and infiltrated bases in disguise. He founded FOXHOUND, Militaires Sans Frontières, Outer Heaven and Zanzibar Land, and was finally defeated by Solid Snake.

techniques: CQC, matching The Boss's mastery in their final duel
Marksmanship, including urban and maritime sniping
Hand-to-hand combat

mechanisms: Disguises and concealment, including the cardboard box

weaknesses: Underestimates opponents: lost to an initially unarmed Solid Snake in Zanzibar Land, and misjudged Chico in Peace Walker
Lost his right eye to Ocelot's gunfire
limitations: Ordinary human: badly burned in Zanzibar Land and left in a coma for nine years

sources.supports: CQC, sniping, disguised infiltration, torture resilience, fights with The Boss, Ocelot, Volgin, Gray Fox and Solid Snake, the organizations he founded, and the distinction from Venom Snake

feats.claim: Incapacitated The Boss in their final duel, his CQC by then matching hers
Infiltrated Graniny Gorki disguised as a scientist and Groznyj Grad in a stolen officer's uniform
Founded FOXHOUND and Militaires Sans Frontières, and established Outer Heaven and Zanzibar Land

notableResults.citation: Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater
Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater, Groznyj Grad
Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, Zanzibar Land
Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater
Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, Zanzibar Land
notableResults.note: Underestimated an unarmed Snake; defeated with a makeshift flamethrower

campaignTags.claim: Infiltrated Graniny Gorki disguised as a scientist and Groznyj Grad in a stolen officer's uniform

unknowns: Cybernetic parts: the page only says he was rumored to have received them from Dr. Madnar after Outer Heaven

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): removed Gemini's stun arm and Fulton recovery, which are Venom Snake's MGSV gear and belong to a different person. Also removed: tranquilizer marksmanship, stealth camouflage, combat roll and tactical cover. The Outer Heaven loss was Venom Snake's, so it is not recorded here. `stealth` is narrowed to `infiltration`; `gadgets` and `tech` were removed. Page read to about 100k of 170k characters.

characters.summary: The red ghost, nicknamed Shadow: the most persistent and aggressive of the four ghosts. In chase mode he always targets Pac-Man directly, and he accelerates continuously as Cruise Elroy once enough dots are eaten.

techniques: Direct pursuit: always targets Pac-Man's position in chase mode
Cruise Elroy: continuous acceleration after Pac-Man eats a set number of dots

mechanisms: Not established by the cited source

weaknesses: After Pac-Man eats a Power Pellet he can be eaten; trying to flee does not save him
limitations: In scatter mode he retreats toward the top-right corner instead of chasing

sources.supports: Chase and scatter behavior, Cruise Elroy, and vulnerability after a Power Pellet in the arcade original

feats.claim: Most persistent and aggressive of the original four ghosts, accelerating continuously as Cruise Elroy

notableResults.citation: Pac-Man (1980)
notableResults.note: Eaten after Pac-Man takes a Power Pellet

unknowns: Whether ghosts are intangible: the page does not say
Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Gemini's intangibility defense, maze-bound limitation, floating mobility and 'hundreds of mazes' feat are unsupported. They were replaced with what the page states.

characters.summary: King of the Koopas, portrayed with great physical strength. He breathes fire in many forms, attacks with his spiked shell and ground pounds, and uses dark magic. Mario defeats him constantly.

techniques: Fire breath: continuous flares, fireball flurries, blue homing flames
Spiked-shell spins and rolls
Ground pound, punches, stomps and body slams
Dark magic (turned Mushroom Kingdom citizens into blocks)
Lightning (Hotel Mario, Super Mario Galaxy opening)

mechanisms: Great physical strength and mass; one pamphlet gives his weight as 10 tons
Resistant to lava in some games (New Super Mario Bros. Wii)

weaknesses: Lava defeats him in many games, including the original Super Mario Bros.
limitations: His size varies widely by game: about twice Mario's height usually, but up to five times in Super Mario Odyssey

sources.supports: Strength, fire breath, shell attacks, ground pound, dark magic, lightning, teleportation, size and weight, lava vulnerability, and his constant defeats by Mario

feats.claim: Breaks boulders and topples enemies many times his size
Used dark magic to turn Mushroom Kingdom citizens into blocks and other items

notableResults.citation: Super Mario series (e.g. Super Mario Odyssey ending)

campaignTags.claim: Breathes continuous flares, fireball flurries and homing flames
Used dark magic to turn citizens into blocks (Super Mario Bros. booklet)
The page states he can teleport
Shows lightning powers in Hotel Mario and the Super Mario Galaxy opening

unknowns: Height in feet is not documented on the page, so giant-sized is not proposed under the owner's 8 ft ruling
Koopa Clown Car flight is not mentioned in the portion read

Reviewed by Claude (2026-11-13): Gemini's giant-sized claim ('well over eight feet') is not in the source, so the tag was removed. Also removed: 'low agility', Clown Car flight, and the bridge-switch note. The broad `fire` and `magic` tags are narrowed to `fire-control` and `spellcaster`; `self-teleport` and `electric-control` were added. Page read to about 100k of 557k characters.

techniques: Giant rainbow fireballs; clones himself to double them
Giant hammer strike
Grows to giant size and chases with fire streams and shockwaves
Summons the Shy Guy Airtub DX
Summons Dreamy Goombas, Shy Guys, Bob-ombs and Paratroopas

mechanisms: Right arm blocks attacks to his head; left arm grabs a brother
Regenerates 200 HP per arm and 150 HP on his body each turn while in the background

weaknesses: Weak to Jump, Bye-Bye Cannon, Dropchopper and Star Rocket
Defeat makes him expel the Dream Stone's remains, leaving him weakened in normal form
limitations: The form depends on the Dream Stone's remains inside him

feats.claim: Grew to giant size and cloned himself during the final battle

notableResults.citation: Mario & Luigi: Dream Team, Neo Bowser Castle balcony

Regenerates arm and body HP each turn while in the background
